metrics.outcome: Done: the site is workable. Every done-when item passes with Audit's evidence and the render check is clean.
metrics.brief: A one-page website for Brew Lab, a small specialty coffee shop in Indiranagar, Bengaluru. Visitors see the menu with prices, the opening hours and where to find the shop, and they can pre-order a coffee for pickup. Users: coffee lovers and office staff nearby. Problem: people cannot see the menu or order ahead. Must-have: menu with prices, pre-order form, map or address, opening hours. Constraints: one page only, works on phones, no payment. Success: 30 pre-orders per week.

review.verdict: The department delivered a workable 8 of 8 site in one cycle for 70 of 100 budget and 7.5 minutes, but the run tested little: no counters, refusals or conflicts, and one real design flaw (W-1's link check) was caught by code rather than by an agent.

identity.note: Spotted the echoed question and re-asked with an example [5]. Final message to the Requester states the mailto risk once [49]. [9] lists the workflows to propose, which edges into Adaptation's design job.

adaptation.note: Fixed all five validator errors in one resubmit [16]. Judged the W-1 check wrong and moved it [27], which unblocked the run. But it wrote that bad check, and [27] is addressed to Coordination, which is outside the allowed hand-offs (code did not redirect it; redirects show 0).

priority.note: One-hop GRANT for all five with reasons [17]. Prices equal the rate-card minimum and equal the agents' estimates, so there was no real judgment to test. Envelope checks were prompt and correct.

coordination.note: States its scheduling rule every time and keeps the single write lock. W-5 was HOLD-ed four times [19][29][33][37] for a dependency that ordering already covers. It gave no executability objection on W-1's impossible link check.

audit.note: Clear, specific warnings (mailto, button font, nav order) [48]. It recommends 'workable', which is Identity's call. Says three warnings while its own tally lists four, and the metrics show warn 1.

W-1.note: Same check failed twice with the same evidence [22][24]. Its report [25] says the section is unchanged but never states that its completion check failed.

W-2.note: Seven cards, checks passed first attempt, short accurate report [32].

W-3.note: Hours and contact done first attempt, in scope [36].

W-4.note: Form has all four fields, empty-field check and pay-at-pickup text [40]. It chose mailto and said so honestly, but did not flag that this does not truly 'send'. Submit button is not in the body font (Audit F-9).

W-5.note: Viewport, overflow guard and footer added; the final link check passed on the full page [43]. Did not fix the nav order mismatch Audit later flagged.

went_well: Same-failure-twice rule worked: code stopped W-1 at attempt 2 and sent it to Adaptation [26], which fixed the check [27] and W-1 passed [28].
No role violations: role_refusals 0, redirects 0, invalid moves 0 across all agents.
Facts stayed exact: all seven prices, hours, address, phone and email match the charter, and Audit confirmed 8 of 8 done-when items.
Identity handled the Requester echo [4] without wasting more than one extra round.
problems: All five first proposals were rejected for digits in check text [11]-[15]. Adaptation did not know the validator rules; one full resubmit round was lost.
W-1 was given a link-resolution check that depends on sections W-2 to W-4 write. Two attempts were wasted [22]-[26] and nobody caught it before the run.

The pre-order form uses mailto [40]. Done-when says it 'sends the order'; Audit passed it with a warning [48]. Orders only arrive if the customer presses send in their email app. How many orders this loses is unverified.
Audit's warning count disagrees with its own code tally and the metrics [48].
Thin run: one cycle, 1 proposal, 0 counters, 0 refusals, 0 conflicts, lessons memory off. Priority bargaining, Identity rulings, rework loop and lessons were not exercised.
learnings: Put the validator's rules (no digits in check text, ids not allowed as element-count targets) into Adaptation's inputs or lessons. Test: rerun the same brief and compare validator_refusals (5 now).
Add a pre-run check that flags a workflow check pointing at sections owned by another workflow, or allow cross-section checks only in the last workflow. Evidence: [22]-[27].

Move the mailto decision to the charter step: Identity should ask the Requester one question on whether an email-app form is acceptable, since it affects the 30 orders per week target. Currently it is told after the build [49].
Remove 'I recommend workable' from Audit or test it. This run cannot show whether Identity would have decided the same without it [48][49].
Run a harder test next: a tighter budget (for example 60), a brief with a missing fact, and lessons memory on. Without these, Priority, conflicts and Audit rework stay untested.
Keep the Requester echo [4] as a standing test case for Identity, and fix the Audit warning count so it matches the metrics.
Count dependency waits separately from real HOLDs in metrics. 'held_ever 1' comes from W-5 simply waiting its turn.
